terra.problem: The closing line is generic and sentimental rather than sounding like Papa Dorin.
The joke gives Papa Dorin feet and has him trip over his mustache. His gold base is part of him.
The second-helping joke makes light of God's attention to Cornelius. Humor should not target God.
The passage says what the man in radiant clothing told Cornelius, but does not say that God spoke through the man.
The passage does not identify the gathered people's nation or say they were all from a nation other than Peter's.
Saying everything good in the verse traces back to God being with Jesus extends Peter's stated reason beyond what he says.
Peter says Jesus was seen by chosen witnesses, not by all the people. He does not say the witnesses were not a crowd.
The claim that Cornelius and his friends heard this at the same moment the rest of us would is unsupported and unclear.
The Spirit fell while Peter was still speaking. The text does not say he had no chance to finish.
Saying surprise is why they were stunned is circular and adds no explanation.
Peter says they received the Spirit just as the believers had. Saying there was no difference in the way it happened goes beyond his words.
The text says they asked Peter to stay for a few days, not that he stayed or that the stay would last that long.
